suggestion: Automate game-book text extraction on the scheduled runner so quarter scores and per-player logs land without session transcription.
why: The job already downloads every finished game's book PDF; the feed and the minutes model currently wait for an agent to transcribe each book.
options: A) pypdf/pdfminer extraction on the runner + the existing arithmetic-identity gates (points sum == team final) before any row is ingested; B) keep agent transcription only; C) licensed data feed.
recommended_option: A, with B as the fallback whenever an extraction fails its identity gate (the row stays blank and flagged — never repaired).
dependency: runner Python packages; the identity gates already exist in scripts/parse_gamebook.py and scripts/results_feed.py.
decision: pending — reviewer picks the path before implementation

suggestion: Capture the official standings page on the scheduled runner (fetch + parse) instead of deriving records from game-page JSON alone.
why: The derived snapshot carries W-L only; the standings page adds division, home/road, streak and GB columns that the model and the pages use.
options: A) scheduled fetch of nba.com/standings with an HTML parser; B) derive W-L only (current automation) + periodic session captures (current complement); C) licensed feed.
recommended_option: B short-term (already live), A when the runner's HTML fetch can be validated against a stored capture.
dependency: the runner fetches raw HTML whose structure could not be inspected from the capture sandbox — validate before trusting (never infer).
decision: pending — reviewer picks the path before implementation

suggestion: Capture closing lines (a licensed odds source) to set the closing line's weight by its measured out-of-sample log-loss, as the brief specifies.
why: Without closing lines the prior prints the model line alone and the market anchor is shown missing (Q-4C69-03).
options: A) licensed odds API with pre-tip and closing snapshots; B) manual pre-tip capture by the session agent; C) leave the anchor empty and flagged (current).
recommended_option: A when licensed; C until then — the brief's no-inference rule forbids reconstructing a closing line from model output.
dependency: odds data licensing (ties into the NBA terms question Q-4C69-01).
decision: pending — reviewer picks the path before implementation

suggestion: Adopt a jury pass: two independent re-reads of every published final before settlement, recorded as separate votes in the capture file.
why: The 11/15 settlement already used two reads per game (game book + scoreboard) and caught the ATL@MIL quarter conflict because of it.
options: A) formalise double-read as a settlement gate (cheap, offline); B) keep the practice informal; C) single read with spot checks.
recommended_option: A — the gate is a few lines in scripts/results_feed.py settle and turns the practice into an enforced invariant.
